finalText:
**Found it — `processOrder` leaked a connection every time an order failed.**

It called `pool.acquire()`, then `await run(...)`, then `pool.release(conn)`. When `run` rejected, the release line never ran. The pool has no reclaim, so each bad order burned a slot permanently.

The worker log proves it: 125 jobs started, 120 released, 5 failed. Pool size is 5. The fifth bad order at `02:06:30` took the last slot, and everything after got `pool exhausted`.

The API path was never at fault. `handleRequest` uses `withConnection`, which releases in a `finally`. It just starved on the same drained pool.

The fix routes `processOrder` through `withConnection` too. The comment about needing the connection across a retry loop is stale — that loop is gone.

All 4 tests pass, 69ms.
